translation:
True Huangdan (5 liang; grind fine and levigate in water, wait for it to dry, place it in thick silk paper, stir-fry it in a pot until cooked, take it up, set it on the ground to cool, then stir-fry and cool again in this way nine times, completely removing the lead qi, then grind again like dust, and set aside for use). Chuan Huanglian (remove the root and clean, 2 liang, cut into pieces). Shiyan (one female and one male; the large ones are like betel nuts, equal parts with Shixie, pound into powder and levigate in water, set aside for use). Shixie (whether one or two pieces, equal parts with the male and female Shiyan, pound into powder and levigate in water). Hezi (twelve pieces). True bear gall (3 qian or 5 qian; the more, the faster the effect. The test method: scatter dust on the surface of water, take a millet-grain's worth and drop it on the water; if the dust separates, it is genuine. This is a divine product among eye medicines). Winter white honey (strained and cleaned, 8 liang).

First decoct the Huanglian and Hezi in three bowls of well water down to one and a half bowls. Make the Xies and Yans into fine powder, levigate in water, and blend with the medicinal juice together with the honey. In a silver pot over a slow fire, boil for three to five bubbles, then add the Huangdan and boil again. Take a willow branch or a peach and locust branch, and stir continuously in one direction without stopping the hand, keeping a basin of water at the side. If it boils up, immediately lift the pot and set it in the water basin. Wait until the medicine forms threads, then add the bear gall and stir again for over a hundred turns. Do not let chickens, dogs, living persons, or women see it. This formula specializes in treating all eye diseases of men and women; even those whose two eyes have not seen for more than ten years can finally regain their sight. But use about two clam-shells' worth, applying it five, seven, or nine times daily, and do not apply to both eyes at once. After applying for the first seven days, stop for three to five days, then apply for another seven days, and use a lamp-wick to wipe away the films; the eye will become bright by itself. For severe cases, it is divinely effective within no more than twenty-one days.
translator_notes: 真黃丹 (true Huangdan) refers to high-quality lead oxide (litharge).
石燕 (Shiyan) and 石蟹 (Shixie) are mineral medicines used for eye disease.
兩蛤許 (about two clam-shells' worth) appears to denote a quantity but the exact amount cannot be confirmed.
燈草榐翳膜 (wiping the film with a lamp-wick) refers to a procedure of wiping away the film with a lamp-wick.
